recordDecisions.title: Failure of direct finiteness for group algebras in every odd characteristic
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For every odd prime p p , we construct a finitely presented group G p G_{p} and elements a , b , c ∈ 𝔽 p ​ [ G p ] a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_{p}[G_{p}] such that a ​ b = 1 ab=1 , a ​ c = 0 ac=0 , and c ≠ 0 c\neq 0 . Thus 𝔽 p ​ [ G p ] \mathbb{F}_{p}[G_{p}] , and the group algebra over every field of characteristic p p , fails to be directly finite. The construction combines a single exceptional self-product pair with signed bipartite cancellation. New integer matching data realize the exceptional self-intersection while retaining a strict squared-word decay estimate. We verify the adaptations needed for the earlier bounded-path and planar-localization arguments. A minimal disk picture protects the identity coefficient of c c , so the proof does not require torsion-freeness.

recordDecisions.title: Optimization of the second Robin eigenvalue on a planar exterior domain under fixed area constraint
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We consider the Robin Laplacian on a planar exterior domain with a negative boundary parameter. For a negative boundary parameter of a sufficiently large absolute value this operator has at least two negative eigenvalues below the bottom of the essential spectrum. We prove that under a fixed area constraint and convexity assumption on the bounded complement of the exterior domain the second Robin eigenvalue is maximized by the exterior of the disk. The inequality is strict for every exterior of a non-circular domain whenever the comparison disk has a negative second eigenvalue. The proof modifies the parallel-coordinate method by allowing the angular phase of a trial function to vary with the distance from the boundary. This result resolves the first item in [ KL24 , Conjecture 1.2] by the authors under an additional convexity assumption. Relaxing the convexity and the perimeter constraint remain open problems.

recordDecisions.title: Sheaves on nodal singularities I
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We study two families of moduli spaces of sheaves attached to the node, namely the punctual Hilbert schemes of the non-reduced plane curve x u ​ y v = 0 x^{u}y^{v}=0 , and the punctual Quot schemes of the module 𝕜 ​ [ [ x ] ] u ⊕ 𝕜 ​ [ [ y ] ] v \Bbbk[[x]]^{u}\oplus\Bbbk[[y]]^{v} over the reduced node x ​ y = 0 xy=0 . We compute their motivic generating functions for all u , v u,v and over every field. Both are specializations of a single rational function whose numerator counts matrices by rank, and they are related by the substitution 𝕃 ↦ Q ​ 𝕃 \mathbb{L}\mapsto Q\mathbb{L} . This proves the Hilb–Quot correspondence for the node with independent ranks on the two branches. The main geometric ingredient is an elementary modification of an ideal along a branch of the curve, whose fibres are affine spaces of dimension equal to a contact length. We also construct stratifications of the Hilbert schemes into products of affine spaces and tori, and we formulate a branchwise Hilb–Quot–HOMFLY conjecture, which we test on the colored Hopf link.

recordDecisions.title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi–Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg’s universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.

recordDecisions.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla’s special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of [ 2 , Remark 2.4] , pointed out by Bruinier–Zuffetti [ 5 ] . Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily–Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

recordDecisions.title: Order Maintenance in Worst-Case Constant Time, Verified
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Order maintenance asks for a data structure that keeps a sequence of elements under insertions and deletions and tells which of two elements comes first. We give an algorithm that performs each operation in worst-case constant time, and verify it in Lean 4. The difficulty is to change labels gradually while queries and further insertions continue. The algorithm, assembled from published components, never relabels the members of a full unit in place: they move into fresh neighbouring units. Small groups keep element labels short; groups are collected into larger chunks, which keep accepting insertions while they wait their turn for a shared top tree; and the top tree never changes a label it has assigned. We implement the algorithm as a program for a random-access machine (RAM) deeply embedded in Lean, whose interpreter counts every instruction and allocates a zero-filled array in one step, and prove that the program answers every query as a simple reference specification does and that each operation takes at most a fixed number of steps, independent of the number of elements and of the history. The machine treats arithmetic on unbounded natural numbers as one step, and on such a machine a step bound alone is weak, so we also prove that after t t operations no value the machine has computed has more than O ⁡ ( log ⁡ t ) O(\log t) bits, and that the program runs unchanged, with the same answers and step counts, on a machine whose words have that many bits. A verified translation through an intermediate language connects the high-level proofs to the machine program and preserves step counts exactly, so the interpreter is the only cost model to trust; the development has about 78,000 lines of Lean. Rust code transpiled from the program agrees with the machine semantics on all tested traces, and an unverified native implementation shows the algorithm’s practical cost.

recordDecisions.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang’s descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, Kähler–Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture.

recordDecisions.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

recordDecisions.title: Meromorphic order from Taylor coefficients, least singular values of Hankel matrices and rational approximants
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We introduce a natural notion of generalized order for entire and meromorphic functions and express it in terms of their Taylor coefficients. More precisely, one formula uses the least singular values of Hankel matrices of the coefficients, and the other uses their determinants. These formulas generalize the classical coefficient formula for the order of entire functions and its extensions by Edrei and Sheremeta. The proof combines a theorem of Pommerenke with a bound for the Nevanlinna characteristic that results from a convergence theorem for rational approximants introduced by Prokhorov. We also characterize the largest class of growth scales for which the associated generalized order is well-behaved.

Complete finite tables cover smaller orders. The proofs combine degree and support bounds, local strategy composition, protected routing, and constructions in the missing-arc graph. recordDecisions.title: On the Tur\'an Number of the Cartesian Product of Two Stars
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We study the Turán number of the Cartesian product of two stars, a family whose order of magnitude is known. For most pairs of star sizes, we determine the leading coefficient exactly. In the remaining congruence class, we give explicit lower and upper bounds for the coefficient at the leading scale. Our lower bounds use blowups of polarity graphs, and our upper bounds use structural estimates on neighbourhoods.

recordDecisions.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond . Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset B 1 + ⋯ + B k B_{1}+\dots+B_{k} of k k infinite sets, for every k k ; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host–Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets B + m ​ B B+mB , on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form B i 1 + ⋯ + B i m B_{i_{1}}+\dots+B_{i_{m}} with B i B_{i} drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in ℕ \mathbb{N} and ℚ \mathbb{Q} , and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radić, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets A ⊂ ℕ A\subset\mathbb{N} such that B + B + t ⊄ A B+B+t\not\subset A for every infinite B ⊂ ℕ B\subset\mathbb{N} and every t ≥ 0 t\geq 0 (respectively B + B ⊄ A B+B\not\subset A for every infinite B B ) is 1 / 2 1/2 (respectively 3 / 4 3/4 ). recordDecisions.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz’s graph-energy conjecture.

recordDecisions.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We prove that the three-dimensional chiral ℤ p \mathbb{Z}_{p} Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun–Yang–Wang–Tantivasadakarn–Chen are, for every odd prime p p , not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

recordDecisions.title: Division and noetherianity in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . We show that the local rings of quasianalytic Denjoy–Carleman classes need not be Noetherian. More precisely, we construct quasianalytic Denjoy–Carleman classes C M C^{M} whose local rings C M ​ ( ℝ d , 0 ) C^{M}(\mathbb{R}^{d},0) are not Noetherian for any d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 . Conversely, we exhibit quasianalytic classes whose local rings in dimension two are regular and Noetherian. Our approach is based on the problem of exact division: if f = φ ​ g f=\varphi g , where f ∈ C M f\in C^{M} , φ \varphi is real-analytic, and g ∈ C ∞ g\in C^{\infty} , under which conditions does it follow that g ∈ C M g\in C^{M} ? We introduce a quantitative scale-growth condition on the defining weight sequence M M and prove that exact division holds in two variables whenever this condition is sufficiently strong relative to the rate at which the nonreal branches of the complex zero set of φ \varphi approach the real plane. We also construct quasianalytic weight sequences with prescribed growth thresholds and establish corresponding counterexamples to exact division. These yield nonclosed principal ideals and, consequently, non-Noetherian local rings.

recordDecisions.title: Thin ends and topological spanning trees
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: . Halin conjectured in 1964 that every connected graph has an end-faithful spanning tree. He proved this for countable graphs, but in the early 1990s Seymour and Thomas and, independently, Thomassen found uncountable counterexamples. Both are infinitely connected and hence one-ended, and their unique end has uncountable degree (i.e. contains uncountably many pairwise disjoint rays). Several authors have since asked how much of the conjecture survives. Diestel asked in 1992 whether a graph has an end-faithful spanning tree as soon as all its one-ended connected subgraphs have one; by a theorem of Polat, this would give end-faithful spanning trees in all connected graphs whose ends have countable degree. Diestel and Kühn introduced topological spanning trees, a topological variant of end-faithful spanning trees that exists in every one-ended connected graph, and asked in 2004 whether every connected graph has one. And Carmesin asked in 2019 whether every graph has a spanning tree that is end-faithful at least for its thin ends, the ends of finite degree. We answer all three questions in the negative. We show that the uncountably chromatic graph from an earlier note of ours on a problem of Erdős and Hajnal has only ends of countable degree, each dominated by only countably many vertices, yet it has neither an end-faithful nor a topological spanning tree. A refinement of this graph moreover has no spanning tree that contains a ray from every end of degree 1 1 .

recordDecisions.title: The velocity is deterministic in random walk in 2-valued i.i.d. random environment
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We prove that the limiting velocity for (nearest-neighbour) random walk in i.i.d. random environment is deterministic when the local environment is supported on two points. No ellipticity is assumed. The proof uses a clever adaption (suggested by ChatGPT) of coupling arguments previously developed by the authors. It extends to i.i.d. environments where the local environments are mixtures of two such points.

recordDecisions.title: Classical communication over quantum channels: does entanglement help in nature?
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Can entangling codewords across independent uses of a quantum channel improve the rate of classical communication? An old conjecture states that there is no such entanglement advantage for all channels. Although Hastings’s result and follow-up works disproved this conjecture, it turns out that enormous dimension is required to construct a channel where entanglement enhances classical communication. This indicates that there might be no entanglement advantage for many physical channels, or for all low dimensional channels. Motivated by recent progress on (generalized) amplitude damping channels, we propose a general Schur-weighted block entropy inequality, and show that there is no entanglement advantage for all phase-covariant channels including multi-level amplitude damping channels, generalized dephasing channels, and damping-dephasing channels. As a by-product, we also recover the recently established result that there is no entanglement advantage for all qubit channels.

recordDecisions.title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We give the first polynomial-time algorithm to estimate the partition function of the antiferromagnetic Ising model on the uniformly random d d -regular graph to arbitrarily high accuracy for all inverse temperatures up to the Kesten–Stigum threshold. This is the entire regime in which the model is “replica symmetric”, and is conjectured to be optimal for polynomial-time counting and sampling. To achieve our algorithmic result, we establish the absence of Fisher zeros for the partition function in a constant-width strip around the interval from 0 0 up to the Kesten–Stigum threshold, with high probability over the randomness of the input graph. AI Disclosure The overarching vision and proof architecture were developed solely by the authors without AI input. GPT 5.5 Pro was used, with extensive guidance from the authors, for only a few minor technical aspects of the proof. The authors independently verified correctness and wrote everything by hand. We take full responsibility for its contents. A more detailed statement can be found in Section 1.2 .

recordDecisions.title: Computing Jacobsthal’s Function on Primorials: Exact Values and Constructive Bounds
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Let h(x) = j(Px), where j is Jacobsthal’s function and Px is the product of the first x primes. We describe a parallel residue-covering search. Exhaustive exclusion runs, together with independently checked covering witnesses, establish h(65) = 1134, h(66) = 1160, h(67) = 1192, h(68) = 1216, h(69) = 1248, h(70) = 1274, and h(71) = 1298. Method 5B gives explicit certificates for h(100) ≥ 2054, h(150) ≥ 3558, and h(200) ≥ 5172, using partial coverings with five reserve primes. Exhaustive searches give h(100) ≤ 2798, h(150) ≤ 6898, and h(200) ≤ 11998. The search combines parity compression, descending endpoint restrictions, canonical deduplication, a sliding-window bootstrap, and dynamic prime selection related to Ziller and Morack’s Greedy Permutation Algorithm. We state the conditions needed for capacity bounds and conditional propagation, and organize extensions of complete or partial coverings in a five-tier framework. A catalog of 62 coverings at index 65 supports a verified multi-certificate envelope. The solver source, run evidence, certificates, and arithmetic verifiers are publicly available in the accompanying GitHub release v1.0-paper. Upper-bound conclusions depend on exhaustive execution of the search; the record audits do not independently repeat those searches or supply standalone unsatisfiability certificates

recordDecisions.title: A two-sided criterion for the Riemann hypothesis from weighted prime sums, verified up to 2·10^29
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: For N > 1 let C(N) = 2 Σ_{n<N} Λ(n) n^{-1/2} log(N/n) and M(N) = R(N) − C(N), where R(N) = 8√N − 5.3721834 log N − 7.4013354 + O(N^{-5/2}) is explicit. By a theorem of Suzuki, the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if M(N) ≥ 0 for all large N, and then 0 ≤ M(N) ≤ 4(log ξ)''(1/2) = 0.18484. We prove, with computer assistance, that this two-sided inequality holds for every real 1 < N ≤ 2.15·10^29: up to 10^10 from the primes with correctly rounded arithmetic, and beyond from the first 4520 zeros, certified with ball arithmetic, together with the verification of RH to 3·10^12 and an explicit zero-density estimate. The same ingredients give, for every N and without any hypothesis, −E(N) ≤ M(N) ≤ 0.18484 + E(N) with E(N) explicit and E(10^20) < 3·10^-5. We describe the local minima of M exactly and prove an unconditional energy identity for the slope α(x) = Σ_{n≤x} Λ(n) n^{-1/2} − 2√x + c0/2. We then show that positive weights within q^{δ−1/2} of Λ(q) q^{-1/2} satisfy the energy identity, the prime number theorem and Chebyshev’s identity, yet carry an off-line zero, so any proof must use Λ = μ∗log exactly. We do not prove the Riemann hypothesis.

recordDecisions.title: Maximal Independent Sets in Long Graph Subdivisions
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We study maximal independent sets in finite simple graphs whose edges are replaced by paths with prescribed numbers of internal vertices. Using established finite-state transfer methods, we derive an exact boundary-state formula and an explicit leading asymptotic term that factors over the degrees of the original vertices. A graph-uniform relative error bound gives a sufficient condition for this approximation to remain valid when the base graph grows. Under the same condition, the joint membership indicators of the original vertices approach an explicit product of Bernoulli distributions in total variation. For fixed base graphs, we obtain the first adjacency-sensitive correction and a Gaussian limit for the size of a uniformly chosen maximal independent set. A degree-matched construction demonstrates that bounded aggregate error scale does not suffice for uniform degree-sequence universality. Reproducibility materials include exact enumeration, weighted and moment checks, and numerical spectral comparisons.

recordDecisions.title: A Linear In Rank Bound For Integral Arithmetic Progressions On Elliptic Curves
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Every known bound on the length N of an x-progression on an elliptic curve of rank r has the shape N ≤ C^{1+r}. We prove a bound that is linear in the rank for integral progressions, with an error depending only on the height of the model. Let y^2 = x^3 +a_2x^2 +a_4x+a_6 be an integral model and H_f = 1+|a2|+|a4|+|a6|. For every ε > 0, every integral x-progression of length N satisfies N ≤ (3/2 +ε)s+C_{ε} (1+log(H_f))^{1/2}, where s ≤ r is the rank of the span of the progression. In particular N ≤ (3/2 +o(1))s whenever log H_f = o(N^2). The proof has two halves. The local theory consists of exact point counts, the root-class lemma, pinned values, and a forbidden range of primes reaching N^2/49 by a shift-and-square argument. It forces log |b| ≫ N^2, where b is the common difference. The spectral cap is proved in an exact form. Splitting the Neron–Tate pairing into local kernels of positive type and summing the regularised diagonal terms over all places gives an identity in which the bad-prime corrections cancel. Combined with a uniform archimedean separation lemma, this yields λ_{max}(G) ≤ (3/4) logX + (1/4) ψ(N − 1) + (5/4) log(H_f )+ 2, where X =max|x_i|. Over function fields we prove an exact colouring formula for the Gram matrix of a progression of integral sections, which gives N ≤ min(6χ, (3/2)s). We also classify the 3-term Gram types on rational elliptic surfaces and show that all of them occur, and we show that all sign data are realised on elliptic K3 surfaces. The main bound is vacuous for every known example (all have N ≤14); its interest is that it is linear rather than exponential in the rank.

recordDecisions.title: First-order phase transition in Onsager's model of hard rods in $\mathbb R^3$
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We prove a first-order transition for hard rods in R 3 \mathbb R^3 R 3 whose orientations vary continuously over the sphere. For every sufficiently small positive ratio of diameter to length, the grand-canonical pressure has a nondifferentiable point, with a jump in number density at the intermediate Onsager scale. Following the phase-pressure strategy of Lebowitz, Mazel, and Presutti, we connect coexistence in the homogeneous Onsager functional to the microscopic pressure through an exact auxiliary-field representation, exponential decay of correlations in the rod gas at fixed auxiliary field, and estimates of the free-energy cost of interfaces between connected families of minimizing angular profiles.

recordDecisions.title: Finite Alphabet Communication with Noisy Forward Memory in a Normalized Loop
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We study one-use communication of a finite classical message through a stipulated normalized loop containing a backward binary symmetric channel and one noisy forward memory carrier. The carrier is either a classical bit or a qubit; no shared random seed, retained side register, or entanglement is supplied. For every finite message count, we characterize the qubit optimum by a constructive scalar feasibility test. For rational noise parameters and a rational target success, the test uses O(M²) constant-size rational arithmetic checks. The proof combines an exact decoder reduction, minimum-trace allocation for constant encoders, and a concave geometric cap with a matching polygon construction. For three messages, the qubit and classical-bit optima coincide throughout the allowed noise range; an explicit Bernstein certificate proves the remaining polynomial inequality. For four messages, an exact rational qubit protocol exceeds a bound valid for every classical-bit protocol. These are conditional mathematical results for the declared resource model, not a construction of a physical backward channel. Independent human review and originality assessment remain pending.

recordDecisions.title: Smallest Gaps between Eigenvalues of Wigner Matrices without Smoothness Assumptions
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: We determine the asymptotic distribution of the smallest gaps between eigenvalues in the bulk of the spectrum of real symmetric Wigner matrices, including Bernoulli matrices. After multiplication by N 3 / 2 N^{3/2} N 3/2 , the gaps and their locations converge to a Poisson point process with the same intensity as for the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble. Since changing a single entry can move eigenvalues by an amount comparable to the smallest gaps, standard perturbative comparison estimates do not directly resolve this scale for arbitrary entry distributions. Instead, we use that resampling a few random entries does not change the law of the matrix, and we show that the resampling moves each pair of nearby eigenvalues by a random walk that satisfies a local limit theorem; this requires excluding arithmetic structure in the eigenvectors. We also prove a law of large numbers for the number of gaps at all scales between N − 3 / 2 N^{-3/2} N − 3/2 and N − 1 N^{-1} N − 1 , and we sketch the proof of the analogous smallest-gap result for complex Hermitian Wigner matrices.

recordDecisions.title: The ten minimum universal sets of MacMahon cubes
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: A universal inventory of six-coloured MacMahon cubes can build a 2 by 2 by 2 model of every target variety, using eight distinct physical copies, without requiring internal face colours to match. We prove that the minimum inventory size is twelve and classify all ten labelled inventories attaining it, even when repetitions are allowed. They are exactly the two-triangle sets in Conway's tableau. The proof derives row and column sums of two from usability inequalities, proves symmetry, and eliminates every other degree-two inventory by corner coverage. Finite kernel-checked witnesses establish sufficiency. The formalization also verifies the proper cube rotations, outward faces, and completeness and uniqueness of the thirty geometric representatives.

recordDecisions.title: Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Only the newly reported lattice bound at one direction with a complementary-hyperplane quadratic expansion and its own constants is collected as a possible extension; the published main lattice/continuum fluctuation theorems are not new discoveries of this formalization. A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two papers of S. Armstrong and A. Bou-Rabee on the fluctuations of passage times in first-passage percolation. "Curvature and variance in lattice first-passage percolation": for independent, identically distributed edge weights on Z^d, d >= 2, whose law nu has an exponential moment and nu({0}) below the critical probability of bond percolation (Assumption (W)), and for constants delta in (0, 1], r > 0, Lambda >= 0 and lambda > 0, there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu(x)| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every unit vector xi in R^d, rational or not, at which the time constant mu has a quadratic expansion on the orthogonal hyperplane with these constants (Assumption (Curv): a linear term, a quadratic form at least lambda |h|^2, and a remainder at most Lambda |h|^(2 + delta) for |h| <= r), and every x in Z^d other than 0 within distance |x|^(3/4) of the ray through xi; epsilon and C do not depend on the direction (Theorem 1.1). The repository also proves the variance bound that follows, Var T(0, x) <= 2 C^2 |x|^(1 - epsilon), and Var T(0, floor(n xi)) <= n^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large integer n, uniformly in the direction, the floor taken coordinatewise. "Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation": for the random density psi(chi * W) of Gaussian white noise W on R^d, d >= 2, with chi smooth, radial and supported in the closed unit ball and psi continuous with values between two positive constants, the passage time T over rectifiable curves has a time constant mu = lim t^(-1) E T(0, t e_1), and there are epsilon > 0 and C such that E exp(|T(0, x) - mu |x|| / (C |x|^((1 - epsilon)/2))) <= 2 for every point x with |x| >= 1 (Theorem 1.1); the same holds for every density of white noise or of a homogeneous Poisson process that is jointly measurable, determined by the noise in the closed unit ball around each point, bounded between two positive constants and equivariant under rotations and translations (Assumption A, Theorem 1.2). The repository also proves the variance bounds that follow, Var T(0, t e_1) <= t^(1 - epsilon) for every sufficiently large t and Var T(0, x) <= |x|^(1 - epsilon) for every point x with |x| sufficiently large. Every result of the literature that the proofs cite is stated and proved in the repository.

recordDecisions.title: The orthogonal art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete (point-point and point-boundary), in Lean 4
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g guards is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, both when the guards must see the whole polygon (point-point) and when they must see only its boundary (point-boundary). Both problems also reduce to ETR by formulas whose only variables are the 2g coordinates of the guards. As far as we could determine, hardness for orthogonal polygons was open: it is treated neither by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021) nor by Stade (SoCG 2025). The hardness proof is a new construction derived from Stade's polygon: needles become corridors, wedges become rectangles with needle cutters, the slanted mouths of the copy nooks are kept through helper guards pinned by four-armed crosses, and the addition gadgets are replaced by new orthogonal rooms. Its visibility, pinning and coverage facts are checked by the kernel as certificates (cone propagation with a symbolic height parameter, polynomial sign tests for the copy nooks, coverage by convex items). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

recordDecisions.title: Half-rate prefix clocks for every two-input gate
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Rule 30's right edge, read in the frame that moves with it, is the map x_j -> x_j XOR (x_(j-1) OR x_(j-2)) on binary sequences. Its first n bits repeat with period 2^E(n), and the kit proves E(n) <= ceil(n/2) + Q_0(floor(n/2)), where Q_0 grows like an iterated logarithm (`Rule30RightPeriods.per_upper_half`). We prove that this upper bound does not depend on OR. Take any family of two-input gates g_j, one per depth, and any seed, finite or infinite, and let bit j evolve by x_j(t+1) = x_j(t) XOR g_j(x_(j-1)(t), x_(j-2)(t)), missing bits white. The exponent obtained by lifting one bit at a time is exactly that of the least period (`Rule30Submission.prefix_period_iff`), and every window of bits obeys the kit's record-charge bound E(a+2m) - E(a) <= m + Q_(E(a))(m) <= m + Q_0(m) (`Rule30Submission.prefix_window_bound`, `Rule30Submission.prefix_window_le_B`, `Rule30Submission.prefixExp_le_B`). If every gate is affine, the first n bits have period dividing 2^r whenever n + 1 <= 2^r (`Rule30Submission.affine_prefix_bound`). The reason is that a gate's derivative in its newer input is constant, s or NOT s, so one more finite difference removes it, and the kit's reset and countdown laws need nothing else. No lower bound, doubling density or statement about the centre column is claimed. Later same-package extension: For gates g_j, one per depth, and any seed, bit j of the edge map evolves by x_j(t+1) = x_j(t) XOR g_j(x_(j-1)(t), x_(j-2)(t)), missing bits white; with g = OR this is the right edge of Rule 30. Our earlier submission R30-20261030-7b0d12 proved that the first 2m bits have period 2^E(2m) with E(2m) <= m + Q_0(m), the kit's record-charge bound, which allows the excess E(2m) - m to reach 3 from m = 19. We prove it cannot do so before 2058: E(2m) <= m + 2 for every m < 2058, every gate family and every seed (`Rule30Submission.prefixExp_le_add_two`, `Rule30Submission.first_excess_three`). Three new laws hold for every gate: no three consecutive doublings once the period is at least 2 (`Rule30Submission.no_three`); after a pair whose second bit alone doubles, the next bit doubles exactly when the gate is quadratic and the pair's first bit has odd weight (`Rule30Submission.after01_double_iff`); and after two doublings from period M, the next bit's difference order is at least M - 2 (`Rule30Submission.after11_order`). Choosing the stretch after the last visit to excess 1 before excess 3 first appears, these force two countdowns, of the first bits' order and then of the last bits' resource, which cost at least 2058 pairs together. A computed family, found by search, attains excess 2 from m = 3. Nothing is claimed about excess 3 being reached, about later thresholds or about the centre column.

recordDecisions.title: The longest ether-pair episode behind a black right edge of rule 30
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: Read rule 30 from its rightmost black cell, bit $j$ of the edge code $x$ being the cell $j$ places to its left; $T$ is the kit's edge map. Kit pull request 69 (Troy Lowry, `Rule30EtherGrounding`) defines an ether $\mathrm{ether}(i,t)$ of period 4 in depth and 8 in time, and proves that no two adjacent depths of a black-edge code follow it eventually. Let $L(k)=\lfloor2k/3\rfloor+4-[k\equiv0,2\pmod{6}]$. For every code $x$ with $x_0=1$, every $k\ge1$, phase $(i,q)$ and onset $s$, bits $k$ and $k+1$ of $T^tx$ equal $\mathrm{ether}(i,t+q)$ and $\mathrm{ether}(i+1,t+q)$ on at most $L(k)$ consecutive ticks $t\ge s$ (an episode), and an explicit code $w$ attains $L(k)$, also when cut after bit $k+1$ (`Rule30Submission.episode_max`, `Rule30Submission.episode_bound`, `Rule30Submission.wit_episode`, `Rule30Submission.episode_witness_finite`). If $s+q+2i+6k\equiv7\pmod{8}$, an episode of $L(k)$ ticks forces bits $0,\dots,k+1$ of $T^sx$ to be those of $w$ (`Rule30Submission.witness_unique`). The kit has the frame (`Rule30FrozenRuler`) and a front-and-potential method for the period-three ether (`Rule30EtherThreeErosion`); we found no stated episode bound in the kit, its open pull requests or the submissions. Phillips (2004) explored periodic-background boundary growth experimentally. The front (the deepest mismatch with the ether) at depth $R$ and phase $\psi$ moves by 32 local rules keeping $2R+g(\psi)-3t$ constant from tick 1 on, for a fixed weight $g$, so it advances $3/2$ depth per tick on average. From a floor at tick 1, or along the explicit front of $w$, it reaches depth $k$ by tick $L(k)$. Nothing is claimed for the centre column, the Prize problems, $k=0$, or uniqueness without the congruence.

recordDecisions.title: Finite-Vessel Tape Invariance, Box-Repeat Periodicity, and Non-Halting Propagation on Dyadic Rays

If cell `i : Int` is never visited before step `t`, then `c.tape i = (M.init n).tape i`. Consequently, under `ScansBelow M n t B` every cell `i >= B` equals `(M.init n).tape i`, and under `ScansAbove M n t L` (`L <= 0`) every cell `i < L` is blank (`0`).

2. **Finite-Box Agreement & Repeat Periodicity (`tape_eq_all_of_box_eq`, `run_periodic_of_box_repeat`):** If the head stays inside `[L, B)` up to `t_1 + p` and the configurations at `t_1` and `t_1 + p` agree on `state`, `head`, and the finite box `L <= i < B`, they agree on all of `Int` and `M.run n (t_1 + d + k * p)` has the exact same `state`, `head`, and `tape` as `M.run n (t_1 + d)` for all `k, d : Nat`.

3. **Permanent Spatial Trapping & Dyadic Ray Non-Halting (`not_halts_and_trapped_of_box_repeat`, `not_halts_dyadic_ray_of_box_repeat`):** Any finite-box repeat (`0 < p`) forces non-halting and `[L, B)` confinement for all `t : Nat` across the entire dyadic ray `m % 2^B = n % 2^B` (`m, n >= 2^(B-1)`). recordDecisions.title: Exact Conjugacy Between Rule30SurvivalBridge Frontier Scans and Rule 30 Left Diagonals
recordDecisions.boundedClaim:

recordDecisions.title: Linearity bounds for APN functions — scoped formalization update
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The November1 primary formalization reports: Lean 4 formalization of linearity bounds for almost perfect nonlinear (APN) maps F: 𝔽₂ⁿ → 𝔽₂ⁿ. Write N = 2ⁿ and let L(F) denote the maximum Walsh magnitude over components indexed by nonzero vectors. For n ≥ 5, the formalization establishes L(F) ≤ N − 6, together with L(F) ≤ N − √N/4 − 2 when n is even. For n ≥ 4, ordering the Walsh magnitudes in nonincreasing order as L_k(F) gives L_k(F) ≤ (N/√k)√(1 + (2^(k−1) − 1)/N) for 1 ≤ k ≤ N(N − 1). In particular, L₂(F) ≤ 2⌊N/3⌋ and L₄(F) ≤ N/2. Further bounds relate linearity to the count q of nonplateaued components with nonzero indices. In odd dimension, q > 0 implies L(F)² ≤ N(1 + √(q(N − 1))). In even dimension, whenever 1/2 ≤ C < 1, the condition q ≤ (4C − C² − 1)N/4 + 1 implies L(F) ≤ CN. Additional results sharpen the upper bound on the linearity in certain odd dimensions and constrain the second-largest Walsh magnitude when the linearity is close to N.
